observations: body L1: the dash after «k)» measures 9.5 pt; «40—pag.» has a dash of 9.4 pt.

body L2-L10: formula (α) is al-Battānī's rule of p. 80, L2-L7: the sine of the residue (the cosine of the distance of the Moon from the ascendant) times the sine of the altitude, divided by the sine of the distance, times R, divided by the sine of the zenith distance, that is the cosine of h. It is the rule of the right spherical triangle HET (the right angle at E): the cosine of the angle at H is tan HE : tan HT. «al-Battānī» (L9) has a hyphen (3.0 pt); the label «(α)» stands at the margin and the formula where it is printed.

body L11-L19: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the meridian ABGD (radius 54.2 pt), the horizon BETMD, the vertical circle AHEKG, the ecliptic ZHTL and the arc KLM of the great circle whose pole is H, as arcs of circles fitted to the print (radius 246.1, 264.6, 150.7 and 51.2 pt). The ecliptic ends 0.7 pt short of the meridian at N. The vertical prints broken in places between H and K, the ecliptic where it crosses the vertical at H and the arc KLM next to K; they are drawn whole. The letters are of two types, as far as the scan shows: B, E, T, M, K, N and G upright, A, Z, H, D and L italic; the A is printed without its bar.
body L12, L14: «131–32» has a long dash (5.4 pt). «Ex II» is printed so, with two capitals I; the pole of the arc KLM is H (L13 and the figure).

body L18-L20: L18 is the theorem of Menelaus for the triangle HKL cut by the horizon, which meets HK in E, HL in T and KL produced in M. With HK, HL and KM quadrants, EK = 90° − h, TL = 90° − HT and LM = 90° − KL, where KL measures the angle of latitude, it gives L20 and (α).
body L21: the dash before «De» measures 7.2 pt, shorter than the other dashes of the page.

body L22-L26: the dash after «l)» measures 9.8 pt, the hyphen of «7-9» 3.4 pt. Heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's addition; the dashes before «Falsum» and «Schiaparelli» measure 10.2 and 9.6 pt. The words quoted are p. 80, L7-L9, where the translation has «super horizontem borealem» for the «supra horizontem borealem» printed here.

body L27-L30: «al–Battānī» (L27) and «31–33» (L30) have long dashes (5.5 and 5.2 pt); the dash before «Formulam» measures 10.1 pt. «sed hoc non evenit in ceteris regionibus» is p. 80, L9; the formula of p. 81, L31-L33 is the passage in italics there (note o).

body L31-L35: the dash after «m)» measures 10.1 pt, the hyphen of «37-39» 3.4 pt. The eighteenth part is the reading of Plato; the translation prints «octavam partem» on p. 80, L38, corrected in the addenda (Part I, p. LXXI). The M of «Melius» and «XXX» (L35) print heavy. The sentence goes on to p. 258.
notes_left L1-L2: «p. 82, l. 8-26 et adn. r»: the hyphen measures 3.2 pt.

notes_right L1-L2: the t of «erat» is printed broken and the closing guillemet after «nostris» prints as a single angle; «p. 81, l. 15-18» is the rule for the side of the parallax in latitude («Est denique semper australis in urbibus ...»); the hyphen of «15-18» measures 3.0 pt.
